specs/hal-engine-architecture/spec.md:340:- A round continues only when the model stopped for `tool_use`, named at least one tool, and a `ToolRegistry` is configured ([validated by: continues when the model requested a tool and a registry can run it](../../src/orchestration/orchestratorHelpers.test.ts#L11)).
specs/hal-engine-architecture/spec.md:341:- With no registry configured the loop stops, whatever the model asked for, because nothing could execute the call ([validated by: stops when no registry is configured, whatever the model asked for](../../src/orchestration/orchestratorHelpers.test.ts#L15)).
specs/hal-engine-architecture/spec.md:342:- A `tool_use` stop naming no tool stops the loop, rather than re-querying with nothing to add ([validated by: stops when the model named no tool](../../src/orchestration/orchestratorHelpers.test.ts#L19)).
specs/hal-engine-architecture/spec.md:343:- Any other stop reason ends the loop even when tool calls are pending ([validated by: stops when the model finished for a reason other than tool use](../../src/orchestration/orchestratorHelpers.test.ts#L23)).
diff --git a/specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md b/specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md
index 2749d18..4a4b3db 100644
--- a/specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md
+++ b/specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md
@@ -15,6 +15,8 @@
 - The value the hook returns then replaces the system prompt the provider receives; this is exercised at the orchestrator layer because `HalEngineConfig.provider` takes a `ProviderConfig` and offers no seam to inject a recording provider through config ([validated by: replaces system prompt with returned value](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L221)).
 - For a session that completes without error the hooks fire in the order `beforeSession` → `beforeUserInput` → `afterUserInput` → `beforeModelResponse` → `afterModelResponse` → `afterSession` ([validated by: fires the lifecycle hooks in documented order for a session that completes without error](../../src/config.test.ts#L132)).
 - A `beforeSession` that throws reaches the caller as a rejection, and also runs `onError` with the thrown error and then `afterSession`, because the call sits inside the same `try`/`finally` as the rest of the turn. An `afterSession` hook called under this condition can infer the session never advanced past `beforeSession`: no user-input hooks ran, no model response was generated, and no tool rounds were started — a cleanup hook that allocates in `beforeSession` and frees in `afterSession` will therefore always see the allocation and the release on the same error path ([validated by: runs onError then afterSession when it throws, and still rejects to the caller](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L116)).
+- `afterModelResponse` is called once per user message after the round loop exits and receives the `UsageMetadata` summed across every provider call in that turn, rather than only the final round's usage ([validated by: reports usage summed across every provider call when a turn runs through two tool rounds](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.acceptance.test.ts#L53)).
+- When some rounds in a turn omit `usage`, `afterModelResponse` receives the sum of the rounds that reported it, and when no round in the turn reported `usage`, it receives `undefined` ([validated by: counts the rounds that reported usage when some omit it, and reports undefined when none did](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.acceptance.test.ts#L63)).
 
 ## Engine startup
 
@@ -22,7 +24,6 @@
 
 ## Measured semantics — out of scope
 
-These two properties of `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` are recorded so the hook features that follow specify against real behaviour. This issue changes none of them; each is a separate, out-of-scope change owned by no issue in this epic.
+This property of `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` is recorded so the hook features that follow specify against real behaviour. This issue does not change it; it is a separate, out-of-scope change owned by no issue in this epic.
 
 - The `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error` ([chatOrchestrator.ts#L150](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts#L150)), so a rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string or object — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.
-- `afterModelResponse` is called once per user message after the round loop exits ([chatOrchestrator.ts#L148](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts#L148)), and is passed the `lastUsage` local — the most recent round's usage, not a sum across tool rounds, so a deployer using the hook for billing or audit under-counts every turn that ran tools.

I fixed all four eslint errors in `src/orchestration/orchestratorHelpers.test.ts` and pushed the branch. I did not run eslint, tests or a typecheck here, so CI will be the first check of the push.

- **`max-expects` (line 35):** the test had two `expect` calls. I split it into two tests, "returns the right operand when the left is undefined" and "returns the left operand when the right is undefined".
- **`require-spec-link` (lines 29, 35, 41):** I added four "validated by" bullets under "Whether a round continues" in `specs/hal-engine-architecture/spec.md`. They cover the sum case, each one-sided case and the both-undefined case, and each links to its test at the line where that test now starts.

The branch had not moved past the judged sha. I ran prettier on the test file, and `origin/main` merged as "Already up to date". `git status` shows the branch level with `origin/loop-bench/93`.
